market_holds: Spot $4.54 (sealed baseline, 2026-11-16 18:10 UTC). The Yahoo daily bar closed at $4.59, -12.2% on the day against IWM -1.7%. The 20-day run-in is -18.7% and the stock is -64% from its 52-week high. It has roughly halved since $9.14 on 2026-09-24, the session after the $225m preferred was announced, while IWM fell about 3% over the same stretch, so most of that decline belongs to this company. It ran +28% from 11-06 to 11-11 ($4.76 to $6.08) and then gave back 24% in three sessions into the print. There is no option market, and the only prior reaction is Q2 (2026-08-14 bmo) at +4.34%, which faded about 20% over the following week. Turnover is thin at about 80k shares (~$0.4m) a day; the float is 34m of 74m shares with insiders at about 53%; short interest is about 1.9% of float (stockanalysis/finviz as of 2026-11-16). The guide on record is FY26 Pro Forma Adjusted EBITDA of $60m including $40m of acquired annual EBITDA, reaffirmed 2026-08-14. At that point two deals had closed YTD with only $2.6m of EBITDA, about $30m sat under 10 non-binding LOIs, LTM PF Adj EBITDA was $21.2m, and the guide assumed new capital would be raised. Sell-side targets of $12.88-14 come from 3-4 analysts and are stale. GAAP EPS consensus is about -$0.23, but it means little given large fair-value swings on earnouts and the FPA. By selling off to half its post-preferred level, the price already holds heavy doubt about the $40m acquisition target and the cost of the financing: a 16% cash / 18% PIK preferred on $225m, plus a $130m term loan at SOFR (3% floor) + 9.5%.
view: This print turns on one line: how much acquired EBITDA has closed in 2026 to date, and whether the FY26 guide of $60m PF Adj EBITDA ($40m acquired) is reaffirmed, trimmed or pushed into 2027. Quarterly operations matter less, since organic SME EBITDA grew only 0.4% in Q2. The inputs I can see point both ways. The capital constraint the guide named is now resolved: $222.75m of preferred closed on 09-23, and on 10-16 the i80 facility due December 2026 was repaid with a Sound Point term loan. That should also lift the Q2 10-Q's going-concern doubt, and it frees the preferred cash, which a $150m minimum-cash covenant had locked up until the refinancing. Management had said acquisitions are weighted to Q4, and it closed $15m of EBITDA in Q4 2025, so a release announcing a burst of Q4 closings is plausible. Against that, only $2.6m had closed by mid-August, and deployable capital arrived only in mid-October. To close roughly $37m more by 12/31 the company would need essentially the whole LOI book plus more inside about ten weeks. I find no public trace of any closed acquisition since August, apart from one unverifiable aggregator listing. A trim, or a reframing as 'run-rate by early 2027', is therefore at least as likely as a clean reaffirmation. The price has already halved on exactly that doubt and on the expensive financing, so a trim is largely held, while a reaffirmation backed by named Q4 closings would surprise upward. Persistent supply runs through all of this: a $42.2m prepaid forward purchase agreement and a registered PIPE resale overhang, with no insider open-market buying (the only Forms 4 since August are director RSU grants). The past five sessions' -24% has no company news I can find. I cannot tell whether it is informed selling, FPA/PIPE supply or small-cap tape. Net, I cannot place the deciding line on one side of what the price holds. p_up is near 50, with a large two-sided move expected in a thin, 107%-vol stock.

recommendation.reason: The deciding line is acquired EBITDA closed against the $40m FY26 target and whether the $60m guide holds. I could not observe any closings since August, so I cannot say which side of the price it lands on. The financing risk the guide was conditioned on is resolved, but that has been public since 09-23 and 10-16 and the stock fell 50% through it. The halving appears to price a trim already, which caps the downside, while a reaffirmation with named Q4 closings could squeeze a thin float. Neither side reaches 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: If the release quantifies Q4-to-date closings near $25-35m of acquired EBITDA and reaffirms $60m, I would lean clearly long. If the guide is withdrawn or cut below about $45m, or new equity or preferred is issued, I would lean short despite the decline.

self_critique: Q4 seasonality, freshly freed capital ($222m preferred plus the refinancing), a 10-LOI book signed in August and the Q4 2025 precedent ($15m) together make 'reaffirm with named Q4 closings' more likely than I allow. After a 50% drawdown and a -24% three-day slide on no news, the short-term asymmetry for a thin float favours a gap up. The other side: the -24% slide with no news into the print may be informed or FPA-driven, and a guide pushed into 2027 would land on an equity sitting below a 16% preferred, where even small cuts to EBITDA matter a lot to the common. I do not see either case strongly enough to move off about 50.
approach_notes: P6 (decompose the run-in against IWM) and P4 helped. They showed the halving is company-specific and largely holds the doubt about the guide, which kept me from a reflexive short on the 'missing acquisitions' story.
